chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halaby, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who erred, so he did not know whether he had performed one prostration or two. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should perform another prostration another, and it is not upon him, after the completion of the prayer, to perform the two prostrations of forgetfulness.'

key_terms.سَهَا: To err or make a mistake in worship

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one is unsure whether they performed one or two prostrations in prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the distinction between resolving uncertainty within the prayer structure versus the compensatory rites performed after its conclusion. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that when in doubt between one or two prostrations, the worshipper simply adds one more to settle the doubt, avoiding the need for the separate 'Sajdat al-Fara'igh' (two prostrations of emptiness) required for missing a full rak'ah. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of prioritizing simplicity and avoiding unnecessary burden in acts of worship when doubt arises during the prayer itself.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby who said,

‘Abu Abdullahasws was asked about a man who erred, so he did not know whether he had perform Sajdah with one Sajdah or two. Heasws said: ‘He should perform Sajdah another, and it is not upon him, after the accomplishment of the Salāt, to perform a Sajdah for the omission’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “

Abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was asked about a man who becomes confused and does not know if he has done one or two Sajdah (prostrations). He (the Imam) said, ’He performs another Sajdah (prostration) and after completion of Salah (prayer) two Sajdah (prostration) because of mistake is not necessary.’”
